subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — latency & throughput follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted vs Dedicated — post-call recap and next steps

Hi Alex — great to meet today. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our call so we keep momentum: 

- Summary of your workload: synchronous payment auth and fraud scoring, bursty traffic peaks (up to ~400 TPS) during settlement windows, median request payload ~1.2k tokens, 99th latency target ~120ms per request.
- Key constraint: you need consistent tail latency during peak windows and predictable capacity for compliance reporting.

Based on the above, two options look like best fit: 
1) Hosted API (Redwood Hosted) — fastest to go live, lower ops burden. Good if occasional bursts are tolerable with our autoscale and region routing.
2) Dedicated (reserved GPU pools) — recommended if you need strict predictability on throughput and tight tail latency during peak windows. Dedicated lets you pin model variants, reserve capacity, and get SLA-backed latency/uptime.

Attachments: I attached a short comparison (redwood-deploy-options.pdf) and a template for a mutual action plan.

Proposed next steps: 
- If you want to validate tail latency at scale we can run a short PoC on Dedicated capacity (2–3 days) with your sample load.
- If you want to start with Hosted and evaluate autoscaling behaviour, we can provision an eval key and run a controlled traffic ramp.

Can you confirm which approach you prefer for the PoC? If Dedicated, I will loop in Dev (cc'ed) to scope the infra footprint.

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
Attachment: redwood-deploy-options.pdf (pdf)

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 15:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — post-call recap and next steps

Thanks Marissa — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The 400 TPS number is during a 10–15 minute window twice per day; average TPS is ~40.
- We measure end-to-end latency today at ~90ms (50th) and ~250ms (99th) with our current model stack; our goal is to keep 99th <= 120ms for the auth path.
- Security: we need SOC2 evidence and the option for a VPC/private deployment later on.

Given the tight 99th requirement during spikes, my inclination is to run a short Dedicated PoC to validate tail latencies (we can provide a replay of production traffic). Can you confirm what model footprint we'd need for Dedicated for ~400 TPS peaks (token sizes above)? Also please share expected timeline and cost ballpark for a 3-day PoC.

—Alex
Alex Johnson
Head of Engineering, FinPay
alex.johnson@finpay.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finpay.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 17:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted vs Dedicated — post-call recap and next steps

Hi Alex — great, Dedicated PoC makes sense for validating tail latencies. Quick answers below and next steps: 

- Estimated footprint: for your payload (1.2k tokens median) and target ~400 TPS peaks, we'd recommend a Dedicated pool of 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs with model sharding + quantization profile (we'll run profiling to refine).
- PoC timeline: we can stand up a Dedicated PoC environment within 48 hours of sign-off and run the 72-hour load replay. 
- Cost ballpark: for a short POC we typically price a reserved test cluster at a fixed trial rate (~$6k for the 3-day window) — we can convert to credits if you proceed to a committed Dedicated contract.
- Compliance: we'll include the SOC2 packet and can discuss Private/VPC on next steps; for the PoC Dedicated still keeps data isolated to your pool.

Attachments: finpay-latency-report.xlsx (sample template)

Next steps I propose: 
1) You confirm PoC approval and share a sanitized traffic replay (or sample traces).
2) We get a short SOW signed and I trigger infra provisioning (48h).
3) Run 72h PoC + joint tail-latency review and decision.

If that works, can you confirm by EOD tomorrow and I'll prepare the SOW + PoC pricing sheet.

Thanks,
Marissa
Attachment: finpay-latency-report.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: FinPay — Dedicated PoC next steps (prep)

Internal notes — copying the plan here so we can move quickly once Alex signs off: 

- PoC scope: 4 x A100-equivalent GPUs, model variant: open-llama-7B quantized (initial), profiling to confirm memory/latency.
- Action items:
  - Dev: prep infra template for Dedicated pool and confirm provisioning ETA (target 48h).
  - Neha: draft SOW + PoC pricing (use trial rate $6k). I'll attach the mutual action plan to the HubSpot record and send SOW once Alex confirms.
- Risks: if 99th still >120ms we'll recommend model distillation/parameter swap or move to Private for tighter network isolation.

I'll update HubSpot and drop the SOW draft in shared Drive.

—Marissa
